name: Stranglethorn Vale
summary: Trolls, goblins, pirates, and soldiers contest Stranglethorn Vale. South of Duskwood, the old Gurubashi heartland has become a maze of ruins, beasts, and rival camps.

sections.title: Ruins of an Empire
sections.body: Zul'Gurub once ruled the vale as the Gurubashi Empire's capital. That rule ended when radical priests summoned Hakkar the Soulflayer, and civil war tore through the region. The Zandalari crushed the blood god's uprising, but the empire never recovered. Now successor factions fight across the jungle. The Bloodscalp hold the northwest, while the Skullsplitter occupy the east. Both tribes slaughter outsiders as they fight to reclaim their ancestral home.

sections.title: Pirates and Profiteers
sections.body: Booty Bay fills the vale's southern tip with trade and sea traffic. The Steamwheedle Cartel carved out the port, and the Blackwater Raiders run it under Baron Revilgaz. Bloodsail Buccaneers anchored along the coast keep the port under constant threat. Farther inland, the Venture Company cuts timber and mines the hills for rare singing crystals.

sections.title: A Contested Wilderness
sections.body: Rival powers meet across the vale's dangerous borderland. The Horde holds Grom'gol Base Camp on the western coast, and goblin zeppelins link it to Durotar and Tirisfal Glades. Alliance loyalists at the Rebel Camp hunt for the rogue Colonel Kurzen. In the thick jungle, famed hunter Hemet Nesingwary leads big-game expeditions. Wanderers drawn to his hunts face prowling panthers, enormous apes, and enemy soldiers.

sections.title: The Madness in the Jungle
sections.body: Colonel Kurzen led a Stormwind expedition into the northern jungle, then went mad and built a tyrannical mercenary redoubt. The Mind's Eye, wielded by Mai'Zoth, an ogre mage from the nearby Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound, ensnared Kurzen's mind with sorcery. The expedition fell into madness, and Kurzen's former men broke away to form the Rebel Camp.

faq.answer: No single power controls Stranglethorn Vale. Bloodscalp and Skullsplitter trolls, Kurzen's Compound, the Venture Company, and Horde and Alliance military posts hold rival ground. Booty Bay is the largest settlement, governed by Baron Revilgaz and the Blackwater Raiders.

Booty Bay is a port city on the southern bluffs of the Cape of Stranglethorn. Once the human settlement of Blackwater Cove, it was captured by trolls and later secured by the Steamwheedle Cartel. Baron Revilgaz and Fleet Master Seahorn run it as a neutral trading port, linking travelers with Ratchet across the Great Sea.

faq.q: Why did Colonel Kurzen go rogue?
faq.answer: Colonel Kurzen went rogue after Mai'Zoth, an ogre mage wielding the Mind's Eye, ensnared his mind. Kurzen had led a Stormwind expedition into the jungle, but grew erratic and despotic. Lieutenant Doren and loyal soldiers broke away to form the Rebel Camp and stop him.

Zul'Gurub is the ruined capital of the Gurubashi Empire in northeastern Stranglethorn. Fifteen centuries ago, radical priests summoned Hakkar the Soulflayer there, starting the civil war that ended the empire. Vines and ruins cover the abandoned city, but dark rituals still threaten its halls.

faq.q: What was the Stone of the Tides?
faq.answer: The Stone of the Tides is a legendary relic from ancient Gurubashi history, found on the coast by a troll warrior. It gave its bearer control over water and elemental summons like a powerful mage, earning the name Tidebearer. Its curse slowly drew each bearer from the physical realm until they walked into the sea and vanished.

faq.q: How do I travel to Stranglethorn Vale?
faq.answer: You can walk south from Duskwood across the river border into northern Stranglethorn. Horde zeppelins link Grom'gol Base Camp with Durotar and Tirisfal Glades. From Kalimdor, take the merchant vessel that sails between ratchet in the Barrens and booty bay.

angles.text: As a troll, your ancestral homeland is the jungle troll cradle of Stranglethorn. Civil war followed the Gurubashi Empire's worship of Hakkar the Soulflayer, driving tribes like the Darkspear across the seas.
As Horde, you can rely on Grom'gol Base Camp as a strategic stronghold on the southern continent, supplied by zeppelins from Durotar and the Undercity.
As Alliance, you inherit Stormwind's costly efforts to conquer and pacify the jungle. Now hard-pressed mutineers at the Rebel Camp defend the kingdom's interests.
As a hunter, you can meet famed big-game hunter Hemet Nesingwary on the northern riverbank. He challenges marksmen to track the jungle's fiercest raptors, panthers, and crocolisks.
As a herbalist, you can search the humid canopy's riverbanks and coastlines for Wild Steelbloom, Fadeleaf, Goldthorn, and Purple Lotus.
